subject: Sales discovery: Redwood integration recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.j@acme.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Sales discovery: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Rapid recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Key pain points you confirmed
- High latency and cost on your current document search/assistant flows at scale (esp. 200–500 reqs/sec spikes)
- Need structured outputs for downstream analytics (JSON schema per record)
- Retraining/updating embeddings is manual and slow — you want reranking close to inference time

Goals you shared
- 50% reduction in tail latency and 30% reduction in per-token cost in the first 90 days
- Ability to emit structured JSON outputs from assistant responses for ingestion into your analytics pipeline
- Near-real-time reranking for top-N retrieval results (sub-200ms target)

Product/Integration fit (what we discussed)
- SDK changes: minimal client-side changes — our JS/Go SDK supports chunked streaming and function-calling today; we can add a small helper to map your existing response schema to our structured-output helpers.
- Function calling: use Redwood function-calling to enforce structured JSON outputs and validation before returning to the client. This avoids additional parsing layers on your side.
- Streaming: we’ll stream partial tokens and final structured object; we can setup a websocket or server-sent events path for your real-time UI.
- Embeddings / reranking: we recommend our on-the-fly reranking pipeline (embedding + approximate nearest neighbor + lightweight neural reranker) and a caching layer for top-K results to meet sub-200ms SLOs.

Open items / asks for next week
1) Technical questionnaire — could you send your current request/response size distribution and peak qps for the assistant route?
2) Security: SOC2 evidence & your procurement redlines — I’ve attached a starter pack and the mutual action plan.
3) Decide on pilot scope: we suggest starting with a single assistant route (search+rerank) for November pilot.

Attachments: redwood-integration-proposal.pdf, acme-mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Next steps
- Monica will sync with your engineering lead next week to scope SDK changes and streaming approach.
- I’ll follow up with a tailored pilot plan and estimated committed capacity for Dedicated if you want predictable latency.

Thanks — excited to keep this moving.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0189

Thanks Marissa — very clear summary, appreciate it. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Peak qps: currently ~320 reqs/sec during peak search windows; median payload size for assistant prompts is ~1.6KB, sometimes up to 6KB.
- For structured outputs we need the JSON schema to enforce: {"intent":string, "entities":array, "confidence":number}. Is function-calling able to guarantee schema emergence or do we still need secondary validation?
- Security: we’ve started the procurement loop; procurement asked if you can provide a sample SOC2 report redacted for PII.

We’re aligned on a pilot but would like to include one of our B2B search flows (customer-facing) — would prefer no visible downtime and a toggle switch to rollback.

Can Monica and your engineering reach out to Tom (cc’d) to align on SDK changes? We’re in PST.

Best,
Sarah
Product Lead, Search & Relevance | Acme Corp

Marissa / Monica — quick technical readout: 

- Reranking latency: with the numbers Sarah provided (peak 320 qps, median 1.6KB payload) we can meet sub-200ms for top-10 if we:
  1) use a dedicated small GPU pool for the reranker (T4/RTX-class) and
  2) enable 8-bit quantized reranker model + async embedding cache for top-K candidates.

- SDK changes: minimal. We can expose a streaming helper that emits token diffs + final function-call JSON. On the client side you’d call a single endpoint and handle SSEs; we’ll provide a JS helper that normalizes partials and validates final JSON against the schema.

- Function-calling: function-calling gives a strong structural bias, but we recommend keeping a lightweight JSON validator client-side for safety. We can add server-side validation to the pipeline as an option (we’ll flag failures and route to a fallback).

- Security/SOC2: Monica — please attach the SOC2 redacted bundle to the HubSpot record. We can provide a proof-of-possession certificate and the standard redacted report.

Next steps (technical):
- Monica to produce SDK delta doc + sample code snippets by Tue 11/24.
- I’ll spin up a 2-week pilot config with a small Dedicated pool and provide perf estimates and cost delta.

If this sounds good I’ll loop infra to provision the pilot pool.

-Vivek
